benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Rose to about $114.55 on 23 Oct (Trading Economics), up roughly 8.2% w/w, after a Houthi drone strike killed two near Aramco's Shaybah oilfield on 21 Oct and the US ordered non-emergency diplomats out of Saudi Arabia; Reuters reported Thursday's close was Brent's highest settlement since 4 May. Week-ago is this site's 16 Oct reading, exactly 7 days earlier.

benchmarks.note: Eased further to about $2.73 on 23 Oct (Trading Economics), down roughly 14.2% w/w; pre-crisis is the EIA spot price on 27 Feb (FRED). US LNG feedgas and exports are near records, but the US price stays largely insulated from the Hormuz and Red Sea turmoil.

note: Brent, WTI, TTF and JKM all set fresh highs on 23 October after a Houthi drone strike killed two near Aramco's Shaybah oilfield on 21 October (confirmed, no output impact) and the US ordered non-emergency diplomats out of Saudi Arabia; Reuters said Thursday's close was Brent's highest settlement since 4 May. Henry Hub continued easing, staying largely insulated from the Gulf turmoil.
